page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.2xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor, delivering 8 dedicated virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 32 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and FMA. It is provisioned with 32.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate middle-tier throughput for broader system tests alongside reduced execution rates under intensive compute loads. PassMark CPU testing yielded an average score of 7,041.88, bolstered by extended instruction tests scoring 6,079.67. Potentially uncached large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated stable mid-range behavior, reaching 40.9 GB/sec for read operations and 35.94 GB/sec for write operations. However, stress-ng CPU metrics placed both single-core (1,107.19) and multi-core (5,881.5) output in the bottom quartile. Geekbench scores followed this trend, recording 1,006 in single-core and 3,857 in multi-core evaluations. Compression tasks also showed lower throughput, with single-threaded gzip logging 19.16 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression registering weak results.

Application and synthetic inference tests illustrate bounded efficiency under memory-bound and concurrent compute conditions. Redis operations achieved 5.8 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 6.22 GB/sec, both placing within lower tiers. Lightweight language model evaluation with a 135M model maintained modest rates of 456.64 prompt tokens per second and 117.62 text generation tokens per second. Performance degraded considerably on a 7B parameter model, dropping to 9.74 prompt tokens and 5.29 generation tokens per second.

Given the balanced resource density and dedicated vCPU allocation, the instance provides steady execution for horizontal enterprise microservices, intermediate staging environments, light database workloads, and internal tooling that do not require high single-thread clock speed or local NVMe storage.

Configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an industry-standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage, contains no GPU accelerators, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show balanced large-block memory bandwidth of 40.9 GB/sec read and 35.94 GB/sec write alongside an average PassMark CPU score of 7,041.88. Conversely, Geekbench and stress-ng results fall into lower percentiles, reflecting modest single-threaded compute and compression throughput. This server suits enterprise web serving, microservices, background job workers, and development testing environments.
